summative_rubric.title: Equal Groups Workshop — Summative Rubric
summative_rubric.purpose: End-of-unit rubric covering all 6 expectations B2.1-B2.6. Used to score each child against four levels.

rows.expectation_text: use the properties of addition and subtraction, and the relationships between addition and multiplication and between subtraction and division, to solve problems and check calculations

levels.descriptor: Treats addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division as separate operations; doesn't recognise the partner relationships.
Recognises addition-subtraction partnership with prompts; doesn't yet see multiplication-division pairs.
Independently uses check-by-reversing for addition/subtraction; recognises that 3 × 4 = 12 partners with 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
Articulates the four-fact family for any multiplication triple unprompted; uses the partner relationship to verify both addition/subtraction and multiplication/division.

rows.expectation_text: recall and demonstrate addition facts for numbers up to 20, and related subtraction facts

levels.descriptor: Counts every fact from 1 on fingers; recall is essentially zero for facts above 10.
Fluent on facts to 10; finger-counts facts to 20. Subtraction by count-back.
Fluent on doubles and make-ten facts to 20. Subtraction via fact-family-recall.
Fluent on all facts to 20; produces all four facts in a fact family within 5 seconds.

rows.expectation_text: use mental math strategies, including estimation, to add and subtract whole numbers that add up to no more than 50, and explain the strategies used

levels.descriptor: Defaults to count-all on fingers for sums to 50.
Uses make-ten for sums 11-20; chunks by tens with prompts for sums 21-50.
Independently chunks by tens for sums 21-50; verbalises the strategy.
Combines strategies fluently (e.g., make-ten inside chunk-by-tens for cross-tens sums); estimates to verify.

rows.expectation_text: use objects, diagrams, and equations to represent, describe, and solve situations involving addition and subtraction of whole numbers that add up to no more than 100

levels.descriptor: Can build with objects but cannot draw a tape diagram or write the matching equation.
Identifies problem type with prompts; draws single-rectangle tape diagrams; writes correct equation.
Identifies all three problem types; draws proportionally-correct tape diagram with both parts labeled; writes correct equation; checks by reversing.
Recognises the same tape diagram structure across multiple problem types; solves multi-step problems.

rows.expectation_text: represent multiplication as repeated equal groups, including groups of one half and one fourth, and solve related problems, using various tools and drawings

levels.descriptor: Memorises multiplication facts but cannot demonstrate them as equal groups; treats fractions as whole numbers (e.g., 4 × 1/2 = 8).
Builds equal groups for whole-number multiplication; struggles with half- and fourth-groups.
Builds and writes multiplication for whole-number AND fractional groups (4 × 1/2 = 2; 6 × 1/4 = 1½). Recognises arrays as a second representation.
Connects fractional groups to halving/quartering; volunteers commutativity (4 × 3 = 3 × 4); flexes between equal-groups and array representations.

rows.expectation_text: represent division of up to 12 items as the equal sharing of a quantity, and solve related problems, using various tools and drawings

levels.descriptor: Cannot share fairly; doesn't yet understand division as equal sharing.
Shares fairly when prompted; cannot yet write the division equation independently.
Shares 12 items fairly between 2, 3, 4, or 6 friends; writes the division equation; sees the multiplication partner.
Lists all factor pairs of 12 (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12); writes all four facts of any multiplication-division fact family unprompted.

summative_rubric.usage_notes: Apply this rubric to each child's combined evidence: diagnostic tracker (Lesson 1) + L2/L3/L4 formative trackers + summative worksheet (Lesson 5). The level achieved is the LOWEST of the relevant evidence sources for that expectation.

summative_task_script.title: Lesson 5 Summative Task — Equal Sharing and Fact Families
summative_task_script.purpose: End-of-unit summative assessment. Captures evidence for B2.6 (division as equal sharing) and B2.1 (multiplication-division relationship) explicitly via the worksheet.
administration_steps: Bring children back to the carpet after the small-group rotations on Day 5.
Hold up the worksheet and walk through the four parts: (1) equal sharing, (2) fact-family triangles, (3) sort the stories, (4) how many ways.
Distribute one worksheet per child. Allow 15 minutes for completion.
Walk around and record per-child evidence on the division tracker.
Collect worksheets and score against the rubric: 9-10/10 = Level 4; 7-8 = Level 3; 5-6 = Level 2; 0-4 = Level 1.
summative_task_script.scoring_guidance: Part 1 (3 sharing scenes, score out of 3): captures B2.6 baseline. Part 2 (3 fact-family triangles, score out of 4): captures B2.1 + B2.5 + B2.6 integration. Part 3 (sort 6 stories, score out of 2): captures multiplication-vs-division identification. Part 4 (list ways, score out of 1): captures factor-pair fluency. Total score out of 10.

evidence_per_expectation.B2.1: Lesson 2 formative — check-by-reversing for addition/subtraction; Lesson 5 formative — fact-family triangles for multiplication/division.
evidence_per_expectation.B2.2: Lesson 1 diagnostic — fluent recall for facts to 20.
evidence_per_expectation.B2.3: Lesson 1 diagnostic — chunks by tens for sums 21-50.
evidence_per_expectation.B2.5: Lesson 3 formative — multiplication as equal groups; Lesson 4 formative — half- and fourth-groups.
